text: You'll go to the parlour and wait for me if you know what's good for you. *shakes fist*

# Binding DM ruling for the immediately preceding player message
The resolved mechanics outcome is binding. Use the supplied success and outcome (or degree) exactly as resolved; never recalculate them from the natural roll, modifier, total or DC.

Do not turn this success into another hurdle.","minor_success":"Deliver the intended outcome cleanly.","major_success":"Deliver the intended outcome plus a meaningful bonus or an exaggerated, delightful effect.","critical_success":"Extraordinary success. Make even a gloriously impossible attempt work; embrace absurdity and surprise."}
This game is playful, not a serious simulation. Successful checks must deliver the stated intent: do not secretly refuse, add another check, or replace success with permission to try. Allow stupid, impossible things to happen when the roll succeeds. Scale the flourish and bonus to the degree. Failures should be entertaining setbacks, not dead ends or punishment for creativity. The outcome overrides ordinary plausibility, reluctance, character motives and development-envoy auto-compliance. Never change the dice result or DC after rolling. Decide how the character reacts, not the player's words, thoughts or next action.
Resolved checks: [{"characterId":"player","skill":"intimidation","difficulty":"normal","natural":20,"modifier":17,"total":37,"dc":15,"success":true,"outcome":"critical_success"}]
How to react: Have Oswin start at the fist, then treat the intimidation as utterly effective: he hurries to the parlour to wait, adding a comically precise note that he will choose the chair farthest from the door. Keep the response playful; don’t add resistance or another hurdle.
Play this reaction in your own voice. Do not announce the rules or roll again. Do not use a GM consultation to overturn this outcome. This ruling applies only to that attempt; preserve its established consequences in later turns.

*I start at the fist, then gather my robes with startled efficiency.*

Yes. The parlour. I shall wait in the chair farthest from the door—an old precaution, though usually for entirely different reasons. *I hurry off.*
